content: 1. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Ritonavir can significantly alter estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid coadministration with ethinylestradiol or use an alternative drug. 3. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Ritonavir interacts with etravirine differently depending on the preparation, altering its metabolism. Certain ritonavir preparations (e.g., ritonavir 600 mg BID, tipranavir/ritonavir, fosamprenavir/ritonavir, atazanavir/ritonavir) are contraindicated with etravirine. Coadministration with lopinavir/ritonavir should be done cautiously, as etravirine decreases ritonavir levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. 5. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase everolimus levels or effects by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Lopinavir increases fedratinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the fedratinib dose to 300 mg/day for 2 weeks, then to 400 mg/day as tolerated. 7. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase felbamate levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase fentanyl levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. 9. Lopinavir decreases fexinidazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Ritonavir increases flecainide levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, leading to decreased metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase fluticasone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, such as Cushing syndrome. 12. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase fosamprenavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Ritonavir increases fosaprepitant levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Lopinavir and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Ritonavir increases futibatinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase futibatinib toxicities. 16. Lopinavir and gilteritinib both prolong the QTc interval. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase gilteritinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. 17. Lopinavir and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs during initiation and treatment, and withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or changes by more than 60 ms from baseline. 18. Ritonavir increases glasdegib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases glasdegib levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. 19. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by decreasing metabolism. Avoid coadministration with lopinavir, a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 20. Lopinavir and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ritonavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Lopinavir increases haloperidol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Histrelin increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval and increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Lopinavir increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Hydroxyzine and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Ritonavir increases ibrutinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 27. Lopinavir increases idelalisib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for idelalisib toxicity and adjust dosages as needed. 28. Lopinavir increases imatinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase infigratinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Inotuzumab and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor ECGs and electrolytes before and during treatment. 31. Ritonavir increases irinotecan levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Isoflurane and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Lopinavir increases isradipine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Lopinavir increases itraconazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Ritonavir increases ivosidenib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase the dose to 500 mg daily after at least 5 half-lives of the inhibitor. 36. Ivosidenib and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration with QTc-prolonging drugs. If unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. 37. Ivosidenib decreases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
